rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '4' to '3' on line 17, which is inside the comment '// Load 4 elements at once using float4' → '// Load 3 elements at once using float4'. Comments are stripped during C++ preprocessing before compilation. The actual executable CUDA code (float4 loads, idx calculations, hardsigmoid computations) remains identical between original and mutant.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation only affects a comment string, not executable code. In C/C++/CUDA, comments are removed during the preprocessing stage before compilation occurs. Therefore, the compiled CUDA kernel binary is byte-for-byte identical between the original and mutated versions. The mutation tool incorrectly identified a numeric constant '4' within a comment as a perturbable constant. Since comments have no semantic meaning to the compiler or runtime, no input values can ever produce different outputs between the original and mutant. Layer 2's bitwise comparison correctly shows 100% equivalence across 112 rounds because the actual computation is unchanged.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE - The mutation affects only a comment (line 17 changes '// Load 4 elements...' to '// Load 3 elements...'). Comments are non-executable and stripped during preprocessing, so the compiled kernels are identical. No value-level test can distinguish programs with identical compiled code.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should exclude comments from mutation targets. When analyzing mutation survival, first verify whether the mutation site is in executable code vs. comments, strings, or other non-functional locations. This class of 'comment mutations' will always produce unkillable mutants and wastes testing resources.
